quarterly_data.quarter: AMD press release: Introducing AMD Helion, Agentic AI Compute at Rack Scale (10-12-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: AMD introduced the AMD Helion agentic AI rack, an open blueprint for agentic AI infrastructure based on an Open Compute Project spec-design and powered by AMD compute, in liquid- and air-cooled versions. Example configurations: a CPU-only rack powered by 6th Gen AMD EPYC processors that can support up to 32,768 CPU cores, designed for hyperscale customers (dedicated capacity for agent execution, connected to separate model inference infrastructure); and an all-in-one rack combining AMD EPYC CPU nodes, AMD Instinct MI350P GPU nodes and general-purpose compute for enterprise agentic AI. It includes an integrated token router that directs agents' model calls across frontier and open-source models. AMD plans to contribute the Helion specification to OCP; Helion rack configurations are under development with ecosystem partners and are planned to be available in November 2026. Partners quoted in support of the reference design: Cisco, Dell Technologies (Dell PowerRack), Hon Hai Technology Group, HPE, Lenovo, QCT, Supermicro (to bring Helion to market through its Data Center Building Block Solutions) and Wiwynn. Dan McNamara (SVP & GM, Compute and Enterprise AI): 'Agentic AI is not a single workload ... With AMD Helion, we are bringing AMD EPYC performance, open software and flexible rack designs together so our partners can build systems around customer needs and make efficient use of available power.'
quarterly_data.figure: CPU-only Helion rack: 6th Gen AMD EPYC, up to 32,768 CPU cores; availability planned November 2026
